claims.head: Don’t buy Saros’ record against the Avalanche
claims.body: Saros has been a wall against the Avalanche since 2023-24, well above his usual. But three seasons of data say a goalie’s record against one team tells us nothing about the next meeting, so don’t be surprised if Saros isn’t that wall tonight.

story.head: The Avalanche should pile up the shots
paras: The Predators won the teams’ first meeting this season, 6-2 in Nashville on Oct 25. The Avalanche have won two in a row, and the Predators (5-4-5) beat Tampa Bay 5-4 in a shootout on Saturday. This is a Central Division matchup, with the Preds sixth (tied for 19th in the NHL) and the Avalanche third (tied for 13th).

The Predators keep things calm after the whistle (3rd lowest), get pinned in their own end on long shifts (32nd) and ice the puck a lot (29th). On the other side, the Avalanche do a lot of their shooting from distance (lowest) and get their defensemen shooting (2nd). Colorado has scored 4.21 goals a game, the most in the league. The Avalanche are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against the Predators. On top of that, both teams like to play fast, especially the Avalanche (1st), so expect an open game.

Filip Forsberg (5 G / 12 A / 17 P in 14 GP) leads the Predators in scoring, with nine points in his last five games. Steven Stamkos (8 G / 8 A / 16 P in 14 GP) has a team-high eight goals. Nathan MacKinnon (9 G / 15 A / 24 P in 14 GP) leads the Avalanche in scoring and is tied for fourth in the NHL, with eight points in his last five games and a point in five straight games against Nashville. Artturi Lehkonen (12 G / 5 A / 17 P in 14 GP) has a team-high twelve goals, tied for second in the NHL, with eight points in his last five games.

Juuse Saros (3-3-4 / .902 SV% in 10 GS) will likely start for Nashville, and Mackenzie Blackwood (7-3-0 / .897 SV% in 10 GS) for Colorado. Saros has a .931 save percentage in nine starts against the Avalanche, well above his usual .897. Don’t read much into it: a goalie’s record against one team rarely holds up.
The Avalanche usually control more of the chances than the Predators do.
